\subsection{Mesh dependence of the algebraic residual criterion}
\label{\detokenize{initialization:mesh-dependence-of-the-algebraic-residual-criterion}}
\begin{sphinxadmonition}{important}{Important:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The present algebraic\sphinxhyphen{}initializer acceptance threshold is applied
to the Euclidean norm of a \sphinxstylestrong{finite\sphinxhyphen{}element coefficient residual}.
It is \sphinxstylestrong{not mesh independent}, even though its formula has
no explicit mesh\sphinxhyphen{}size parameter. Do not interpret a lower raw
residual on a finer mesh as a smaller physical constraint defect.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
At a fixed mesh, the current diagnostic checks
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\|F_{a,h}\|_2 \leq \varepsilon_{\rm abs}
+ \varepsilon_{\rm rel}\|F_{a,h}^{(0)}\|_2.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Here \(h\) means the spatial mesh step, \sphinxstylestrong{not} the
fluid\sphinxhyphen{}height state named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{h}} in the shallow\sphinxhyphen{}water model.
The residual entries, number of FE basis functions, weak
integration weights, conditioning and units change on refinement.
For instance, a smooth volume load in two dimensions can yield
a Euclidean residual that scales like the mesh step even when
the underlying physical defect does not decrease.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A future mesh\sphinxhyphen{}aware acceptance test must distinguish:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Algebraic convergence and native GetFEM/PETSc residuals at
each fixed mesh, with solver accuracy checked separately.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Per\sphinxhyphen{}constraint physical residuals}, measured with
suitable dual norms. For an appropriate Riesz/Gram
matrix \(R_{a,h}\), one possible norm is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\|F_{a,h}\|_{V_{a,h}^{\prime}}
  =\sqrt{F_{a,h}^{\mathsf T}R_{a,h}^{-1}F_{a,h}}.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Volume and boundary blocks require their own Gram matrices
and physically meaningful characteristic scales.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Boundary compatibility measured through
\(L^2(\Gamma_h)\) velocity/traction defects, with
appropriate nonzero reference scales.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Refinement studies using consistent physical initial data,
tracking these errors over several spatial mesh sizes.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A physically incompatible \sphinxstyleemphasis{discrete} initial condition must
not be accepted simply because its residual vector becomes
small under refinement. Conversely, finite precision or
a poorly scaled coefficient norm is not a proof of physical
incompatibility.


\subsection{Finite\sphinxhyphen{}difference perturbations and roundoff}
\label{\detokenize{initialization:finite-difference-perturbations-and-roundoff}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The original rectangular shallow\sphinxhyphen{}water example has
fluid heights of order three, density \(\rho=1000\)
and gravity \(g=10\), so the pressure/coenergy variable
is of order \(3\times10^4\). When a normalized
algebraic direction is perturbed with a very small
step \(\delta=10^{-6}\), subtracting nearly equal
assembled residual vectors may amplify roundoff.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first native \#28 shallow\sphinxhyphen{}water Jacobian check returned
a relative difference of \(5.53585698\times10^{-5}\)
for this single small perturbation. This is a numerical
\sphinxstylestrong{failure at that perturbation}, not yet proof of
an incorrect assembled Jacobian.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The follow\sphinxhyphen{}up source\sphinxhyphen{}only diagnostic evaluates central
differences for several step sizes, maintains the
\sphinxstylestrong{original strict tolerance}, checks the independent
affine algebraic identity, and retains a JSON report
even on numerical rejection. Native evidence remains
pending. No production nonlinear initializer is
qualified by this diagnostic alone.

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Energy, powers and time discretization (v1.3.0)}
\label{\detokenize{energy_and_power:energy-powers-and-time-discretization-v1-3-0}}\label{\detokenize{energy_and_power::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter explains what the public SCRIMP post\sphinxhyphen{}processing API \sphinxstylestrong{actually
computes}. The meaning of an energy residual depends on the discrete
Hamiltonian, the port orientations and the \sphinxstylestrong{time integrator}. A successful
PETSc TS solve is not, by itself, a numerical proof of passivity.


\subsection{Hamiltonian: physical value, not a time quadrature}
\label{\detokenize{energy_and_power:hamiltonian-physical-value-not-a-time-quadrature}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
After calling {\hyperref[\detokenize{scrimp:scrimp.dphs.DPHS.solve}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scrimp.dphs.DPHS.solve()}}}}}, the method
{\hyperref[\detokenize{scrimp:scrimp.dphs.DPHS.compute_Hamiltonian}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scrimp.dphs.DPHS.compute\_Hamiltonian()}}}}} evaluates every Hamiltonian
term from the \sphinxstylestrong{genuine stored GetFEM state coefficients} at the corresponding
stored physical time. Expressions and spatial integration regions are those
declared by the user. They are evaluated using GetFEM’s own weak\sphinxhyphen{}form
integration, not by interpolating nodal arrays or fitting a time polynomial.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In v1.3.0, the model time is set for \sphinxstylestrong{every} evaluation. Recomputing a
Hamiltonian replaces the previous history; it never appends a second copy
of the same trajectory. A subsequent solve invalidates the cached values,
and invalid/nonfinite intermediate values cannot be published as a
successfully computed trajectory. This makes the sampling consistent; it
\sphinxstylestrong{does not} imply that the time integrator conserves (or dissipates)
that Hamiltonian exactly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following calls are intended to work in a regular user script:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{system}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{solve}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{system}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute\PYGZus{}Hamiltonian}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{H} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{system}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}Hamiltonian}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{system}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{plot\PYGZus{}Hamiltonian}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}powers}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}figure}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{filename}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Hamiltonian.png}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{show}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{system.set\_output\_name("my\_system")}}, the generated files include
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{outputs/my\_system/png/Hamiltonian.png}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{outputs/my\_system/svg/Hamiltonian.svg}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{outputs/my\_system/npz/Hamiltonian.npz}}. The NumPy file records the
actual time grid, total Hamiltonian, individual Hamiltonian terms and, when
requested, \sphinxstylestrong{raw oriented algebraic\sphinxhyphen{}port powers} and their sampling
conventions. All ranks participate in collective GetFEM work, while
shared figures and data are written only on rank 0.


\subsection{Port powers: raw signs, not universal energy balance}
\label{\detokenize{energy_and_power:port-powers-raw-signs-not-universal-energy-balance}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{scrimp:scrimp.dphs.DPHS.compute_powers}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scrimp.dphs.DPHS.compute\_powers()}}}}} uses the ports’ actual GetFEM
flow\sphinxhyphen{}effort weak products, preserving their declared boundary orientation
and dissipative status. Neither this method nor the integration helper
silently changes the physical sign of a control or an interface port.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a physical model whose sign conventions yield
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}H(t_b)-H(t_a)
= \int_{t_a}^{t_b} \bigl(P_{\rm boundary}(t)
  -D(t)\bigr)\,\mathrm dt,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
the correct assignment of a port to boundary input, output, interconnection
or dissipation is \sphinxstylestrong{model\sphinxhyphen{}specific}. For example, two oriented faces of a
conforming heat\sphinxhyphen{}wave interface have equal exchanged power with opposite
contribution to the total energy balance. A generic port plot cannot
establish that identity without verifying the model’s actual weak forms.


\subsection{Crank\textendash{}Nicolson: only consecutive \sphinxstyleemphasis{accepted} PETSc states}
\label{\detokenize{energy_and_power:crank-nicolson-only-consecutive-accepted-petsc-states}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For PETSc \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ts\_type="cn"}}, SCRIMP uses the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cn\_step}} power convention
\sphinxstylestrong{only if every accepted TS step has its two consecutive end states saved}.
The check uses the real accepted\sphinxhyphen{}step count, the saved times, and (when
time stepping is fixed) the declared \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dt}}. For each step \sphinxtitleref{k \textgreater{}= 1},
the current implementation evaluates the power using the actual
GetFEM coefficient\sphinxhyphen{}space midpoint
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}z_{k-1/2}=\tfrac12\bigl(z_{k-1}+z_k\bigr),\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with the existing SCRIMP convention for the model time, and accumulates
its signed contribution as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}W_{\rm CN}(t_n)
= \sum_{k=1}^{n}(t_k-t_{k-1})P_k^{\rm CN}.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The initial value \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P{[}0{]}}} is \sphinxstylestrong{instantaneous} and is not a previous
step’s work. It does not enter the sum.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a quadratic, time\sphinxhyphen{}independent Hamiltonian with the properly matched
discrete weak forms and constraints, this convention permits the familiar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{model\sphinxhyphen{}specific} exact CN energy\sphinxhyphen{}power identity, up to solver tolerances.
It is \sphinxstylestrong{not universally exact} for nonquadratic Hamiltonians,
time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent constitutive data, or arbitrarily prescribed input
time functions. In particular, one must not mistake a GetFEM evaluation
using the source’s stored time convention for an independent proof that
all time\sphinxhyphen{}dependent forcings were integrated by a midpoint rule.

\sphinxAtStartPar
CN with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_step \textgreater{} dt}} does \sphinxstylestrong{not} provide the adjacent states
needed for each step power. The API therefore switches to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{instantaneous}} samples at each truly stored \sphinxtitleref{(t\_k,z\_k)}
and uses the \sphinxstyleemphasis{approximate nodal trapezoidal integral} below.
It must \sphinxstylestrong{never} label differences between nonconsecutive saved
states as genuine CN step work.


\subsection{BDF, BDF2, ARKIMEX and other PETSc TS types}
\label{\detokenize{energy_and_power:bdf-bdf2-arkimex-and-other-petsc-ts-types}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For non\sphinxhyphen{}CN schemes, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{compute\_powers()}} samples each port
instantaneously at the \sphinxstylestrong{stored} PETSc solution snapshots.
It does not reconstruct derivative histories, hidden stage states,
stage weights, BDF startup steps or solver\sphinxhyphen{}internal quadratures.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default cumulative work drawn by
{\hyperref[\detokenize{scrimp:scrimp.dphs.DPHS.plot_Hamiltonian}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scrimp.dphs.DPHS.plot\_Hamiltonian()}}}}} is the nodal trapezoid
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}W_{\rm trap}(t_n)
= \sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{t_k-t_{k-1}}{2}
  \bigl(P(t_{k-1},z_{k-1})+P(t_k,z_k)\bigr).\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is \sphinxstylestrong{only a post\sphinxhyphen{}processing approximation} to the continuous\sphinxhyphen{}time
work integral. The approximation can differ from the method’s internal
discrete work even when the solution trajectory converges correctly.
With sparse saved states, rapidly varying controls, sharp transients,
stiff or nonlinear dynamics, it can differ noticeably. No general
accuracy order for the energy balance follows from the name BDF2,
the TS solver order, or the trapezoidal sampling formula alone.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In particular:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{BDF/BDF2:} the trapezoidal integral does not implement a BDF
discrete chain rule, G\sphinxhyphen{}stability energy estimate, or the correct
multistep method’s internal work. A quantity displayed as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Balance (legacy port signs; model\sphinxhyphen{}dependent)}} is a \sphinxstylestrong{diagnostic},
not an automatically conserved physical invariant.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ARKIMEX / other Runge\textendash{}Kutta and IMEX methods:} the stored
endpoints are not a substitute for the internal stage values and
Butcher weights. The plotted nodal integral is not an exact
solver\sphinxhyphen{}stage quadrature.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Adaptive stepping or decimated output:} use the true saved
time differences; do not assume they equal the originally
requested fixed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dt}}. If every accepted CN state cannot be
confirmed, the method conservatively selects instantaneous sampling.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To establish an \sphinxstyleemphasis{exact} discrete energy or passivity assertion for a
particular model and time integrator, calculate the corresponding
discrete power balance using the actual method/stage data and verify
it independently. Do not re\sphinxhyphen{}label an approximate generic plot as
a numerical acceptance test.


\subsection{How to inspect the sampling used in a run}
\label{\detokenize{energy_and_power:how-to-inspect-the-sampling-used-in-a-run}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
After \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{system.compute\_powers()}}, the original algebraic ports expose
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{port.get\_power\_sampling()}}, which is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"cn\_step"}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"instantaneous"}}. Inspect their raw \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{port.get\_power()}} time
series and the time grid \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{system.solution{[}"t"{]}}}, or load the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{npz}} saved by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plot\_Hamiltonian()}}.
In the figure, approximate cumulative work is explicitly described as
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nodal trapezoid (approximate)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The source of these conventions is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scrimp/utils/power\_sampling.py}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scrimp/utils/power\_integration.py}}.
Negative tests are in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tests/test\_v130\_user\_output\_power\_hamiltonian.py}}.
For a genuine two\sphinxhyphen{}sided coupled example that makes the oriented powers
and dissipation visible, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{examples/heat_wave::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Heat wave coupling}}}}.

\section{Fully explicit nonlinear bricks}
\label{\detokenize{explicit_bricks:fully-explicit-nonlinear-bricks}}\label{\detokenize{explicit_bricks::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In SCRIMP v1.3.0, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Brick(..., explicit=True)}} means a \sphinxstylestrong{fully
lagged weak\sphinxhyphen{}form forcing}, not merely an omitted Newton derivative.


\subsection{Accepted\sphinxhyphen{}step contract}
\label{\detokenize{explicit_bricks:accepted-step-contract}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For a generic nonlinear weak term \sphinxtitleref{G(t,z)}, SCRIMP’s implicit
PETSc TS residual on the interval starting from the last accepted
state \sphinxtitleref{(t\_n,z\_n)} uses
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}F_{n+1}(z,\dot z) =
M(z)\dot z + R_{\mathrm{implicit}}(t,z)
+ G(t_n,z_n),\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with the sign of \sphinxtitleref{G} determined by the brick’s registered
port\sphinxhyphen{}Hamiltonian form. \sphinxtitleref{G(t\_n,z\_n)} is assembled by GetFEM \sphinxstylestrong{once}
in PETSc’s \sphinxtitleref{PreStep} callback, copied into an owned PETSc RHS
vector, and held constant throughout Newton iterations and
line searches. A rejected time\sphinxhyphen{}step attempt must not update the
explicit forcing from an unaccepted Newton state. After a step
is accepted, the next \sphinxtitleref{PreStep} refreshes the cache from the
new accepted state.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The corresponding implicit Jacobian is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}J = \frac{\partial}{\partial z}
(M(z)\dot z + R_{\mathrm{implicit}}(t,z))
+ \sigma M(z),\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with the additional contracted derivative of \sphinxtitleref{M(z)} in the
state\sphinxhyphen{}dependent\sphinxhyphen{}mass case. There is \sphinxstylestrong{no}
\sphinxtitleref{D\_z G(t,z)} contribution: the cached explicit term does not
depend on the current Newton state.


\subsection{Usage and restrictions}
\label{\detokenize{explicit_bricks:usage-and-restrictions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The original shallow\sphinxhyphen{}water gyroscopic term remains

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{S}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Brick}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{G}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{(Gyro(p) * e\PYGZus{}p) . Test\PYGZus{}p}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{linear}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{explicit}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{position}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{effort}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
SCRIMP’s brick\sphinxhyphen{}registration convention negates the given form
for \sphinxtitleref{explicit=True} (and for flow bricks); the actual GetFEM
registered form and physical sign are unchanged. When
\sphinxtitleref{explicit=True} is requested, SCRIMP requires a \sphinxstylestrong{nonlinear,
non\sphinxhyphen{}\textasciigrave{}dt\textasciigrave{}, non\sphinxhyphen{}source} brick. Other combinations raise an
explicit error instead of silently producing an inconsistent
Jacobian.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cache is distributed in PETSc, and its generic weak\sphinxhyphen{}form
GetFEM RHS follows the calibrated MPI generic\sphinxhyphen{}RHS scaling,
\sphinxstylestrong{not} the special scaling for prescribed source bricks.
\sphinxtitleref{source\_only} and \sphinxtitleref{explicit\_only} are distinct assembly
paths.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Time accuracy:} the explicit term is held at
\sphinxtitleref{(t\_n,z\_n)}. This is generally \sphinxstylestrong{first\sphinxhyphen{}order accurate}
for that contribution even if the main implicit scheme is
Crank\textendash{}Nicolson or BDF2. In particular, the pH power identity
may acquire a splitting or lagging defect; a CN label does
not prove a second\sphinxhyphen{}order or structure\sphinxhyphen{}preserving \sphinxstyleemphasis{combined}
scheme. A second\sphinxhyphen{}order IMEX scheme or extrapolation is a
separate development and requires its own physics tests.


\subsection{Native acceptance}
\label{\detokenize{explicit_bricks:native-acceptance}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The shallow\sphinxhyphen{}water Jacobian regression uses the original
shipped weak forms and a genuinely distinct accepted\sphinxhyphen{}state
vector to freeze a \sphinxstylestrong{nonzero} gyroscopic forcing. It then
checks the production \sphinxtitleref{IFunction} directional derivative
against \sphinxtitleref{IJacobian} for independent \sphinxtitleref{z} and \sphinxtitleref{dot z}
perturbations, and confirms zero drift in the cached RHS
through the Newton/FD evaluations. It compares the default
state\sphinxhyphen{}dependent\sphinxhyphen{}mass correction with the explicit
\sphinxtitleref{legacy} negative control on MPI 1 and 2.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The native gate remains independent of source\sphinxhyphen{}only CI and
must pass before issue \#27 can close:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nv}{SCRIMP\PYGZus{}DOCKER\PYGZus{}NO\PYGZus{}SUDO}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{n+nv}{SCRIMP\PYGZus{}V130\PYGZus{}DAE\PYGZus{}IMAGE}\PYG{o}{=}scrimp\PYGZhy{}mpi:v1.3.0\PYGZhy{}rc3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
bash\PYG{+w}{ }scripts/run\PYGZhy{}v130\PYGZhy{}shallow\PYGZhy{}mass\PYGZhy{}jacobian.sh
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\section{Solver reuse and MPI}
\label{\detokenize{performance:solver-reuse-and-mpi}}\label{\detokenize{performance::doc}}

\subsection{v1.3.0 development candidate}
\label{\detokenize{performance:v1-3-0-development-candidate}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For v1.3.0 SCRIMP focuses on MPI performance without changing the
port\sphinxhyphen{}Hamiltonian model, the PFEM discretization or the Crank\textendash{}Nicolson
time integrator.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default MUMPS reuse policy is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{on\_change}}. SCRIMP examines the
\sphinxstyleemphasis{actual assembled} PETSc preconditioner matrix on every rank:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the stored CSR graph (ownership range, row pointers or column
indices) changes, MUMPS must recompute the symbolic factor.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the graph is unchanged but any stored numeric coefficient differs,
only the numerical factor must be recomputed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If graph and numerical coefficients remain identical on every rank,
the numerical LU can be reused.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This comparison is performed after construction of the actual Jacobian,
including the TS shift applied to the mass matrix and all nonlinear
tangent contributions. Linearity does not imply time invariance: an
adaptive time step can change the operator.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SCRIMP\_MUMPS\_RESET\_POLICY}} remains configurable through
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{on\_change}} (new default), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{always}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{never}}. The older
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{never}} merely avoids explicit PC resets; it does \sphinxstylestrong{not} guarantee
numerical factor reuse.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For MPI LU/MUMPS on more than one rank, SCRIMP also defaults to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ICNTL(28)=2}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ICNTL(29)=0}} (parallel symbolic analysis).
Explicit PETSc options always take precedence, and a one\sphinxhyphen{}rank run
retains the sequential analysis default.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Qualification status:} a previous experimental (not production)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{static\_cn}} benchmark demonstrated one instead of ten numerical
factorizations on ten fixed\sphinxhyphen{}CN wave steps, with matching state\sphinxhyphen{}block
norms. The new production \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{on\_change}} mechanism is different:
it uses exact coefficient comparisons and must pass its own numerical
and MPI regression before the version is released.


\subsection{Reproducible performance qualification}
\label{\detokenize{performance:reproducible-performance-qualification}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
On the validated local Docker image \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scrimp\sphinxhyphen{}mpi:local}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZti{}/Simulations/scrimp
conda\PYG{+w}{ }activate\PYG{+w}{ }scrimp
bash\PYG{+w}{ }sandbox/run\PYGZus{}v130\PYGZus{}wave\PYGZus{}benchmark.sh\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.04\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This executes \sphinxstylestrong{unmodified v1.2.0 sequentially} and the current code
with one, two, four and six MPI ranks, on the same unmodified wave
example, mesh and ten CN time steps (dt=0.002, final time=0.02).
The historical tag is checked out in a temporary Git worktree and
the script refuses to benchmark different wave.py sources.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The current version uses distributed COO, compact matrix memory, and
the \sphinxstyleemphasis{automatic}, unforced MUMPS policy. Both versions use the same
native Docker environment.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The report includes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
model construction, solution and complete wall times, using medians
across independent repeated runs;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
independently measured timing of the first CN step and later steps;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
current GetFEM, bridge, initial consistency and main TS phase timings;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
PETSc symbolic, numerical and triangular solve event counts/times,
with initial consistency and main CN logged separately;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
MPI speedup and efficiency and exact full initial/final vector
comparisons with the release reference.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Human\sphinxhyphen{}readable graphics are written under
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sandbox/outputs/\textless{}run\textgreater{}/png/}}, alongside editable vector versions in
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{svg/}}. Current\sphinxhyphen{}version visualizations include complete solve/total
time, speedup, parallel efficiency, first versus steady CN steps,
SCRIMP phase costs and native PETSc/MUMPS symbolic/numeric/solve times.
The cross\sphinxhyphen{}release sequential bar chart is generated only when full
state parity with v1.2.0 passes. The short current\sphinxhyphen{}only numeric reuse
smoke (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sandbox/run\_v130\_numeric\_reuse\_smoke.sh 0.04 1,2}}) additionally
creates \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{png/01\_smoke\_numeric\_factor\_reuse.png}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{png/02\_smoke\_solve\_time.png}} after all factor and state gates pass.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The runner fails when accepted steps are missing, current MPI
initial/final states disagree, or PETSc native factorization events
do not match the exact graph/coefficient changes recorded collectively
by SCRIMP. A final CN MATCHSTEP shift may differ by floating\sphinxhyphen{}point
roundoff and legitimately produce a second numerical factorization.
No silent numeric tolerance is applied to the reuse decision. If current and native v1.2.0
states disagree, the current MPI scaling report is still valid,
but \sphinxstylestrong{no cross\sphinxhyphen{}version speedup claim is accepted} and the
release timing is excluded from the common scaling graph. Results
are stored under ignored \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sandbox/outputs/}}: Markdown, CSV, JSON
and PNG.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Caution:} SCRIMP phase timers are inclusive; nested phase totals
must not be added together. In particular, the TS time minus its
Python callbacks is \sphinxstyleemphasis{not} solely MUMPS computation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Earlier repeated runs at h=0.01 (744,850 DOFs) showed 21\textendash{}23 \% total
benefit from parallel symbolic MUMPS ordering at 4\textendash{}6 ranks, but still
performed ten numerical factorizations for ten CN steps. Those are
historical measurements and should not be advertised as v1.3.0
numeric\sphinxhyphen{}reuse benchmarks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This performance qualification is separate from the physical
Hamiltonian, input\sphinxhyphen{}port power and dissipative power\sphinxhyphen{}balance regression;
those checks remain mandatory for scientific acceptance.

\section{Examples}
\label{\detokenize{examples:examples}}\label{\detokenize{examples::doc}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{examples:id1}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The examples illustrate both the \sphinxstylestrong{scientific structure} of the
models and the \sphinxstylestrong{practical SCRIMP API}. Start with the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{started::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{first 1D vibrating\sphinxhyphen{}string tutorial}}}}: it
introduces energy variables, co\sphinxhyphen{}energies, outward boundary
tractions, discrete power balance and a real installation check
using MUMPS, serial SuperLU and MPI SuperLU\_DIST.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The examples follow a progression in \sphinxstylestrong{port\sphinxhyphen{}Hamiltonian structure},
rather than a strict ordering by spatial dimension or mathematical
complexity. After the introductory 1D string, the wave and Maxwell
models illustrate distributed linear systems. The finite\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional
mass\textendash{}spring\textendash{}damper and nonlinear pendulum then isolate the roles of
interconnection, dissipation and nonlinear constitutive relations,
without requiring spatial finite elements. The heat equation introduces
the essential algebraic constraints of the mixed diffusion formulation,
before the coupled heat\textendash{}wave and nonlinear shallow\sphinxhyphen{}water models.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The individual pages link to the relevant work in our
{\hyperref[\detokenize{biblio::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{publications}}}}. Their original paper figures are
\sphinxstylestrong{not automatically reproduced} by short installation checks;
each scientific qualification must state its physical model,
solver, mesh (where applicable), accepted time steps and
energy/port\sphinxhyphen{}power evidence.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For interpreting the Hamiltonian plots and the difference between
Crank\textendash{}Nicolson step powers and approximate BDF/ARKIMEX
post\sphinxhyphen{}processing, read {\hyperref[\detokenize{energy_and_power::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Energy, powers and time discretization (v1.3.0)}}}}. The canonical
examples generate their own figures and data under
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{outputs/\textless{}system\_name\textgreater{}/}}.

\subsection{The wave equation — 2A: conservative anisotropic membrane}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave:the-wave-equation-2a-conservative-anisotropic-membrane}}\label{\detokenize{examples/wave::doc}}\index{module@\spxentry{module}!examples.wave@\spxentry{examples.wave}}\index{examples.wave@\spxentry{examples.wave}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{examples/wave:wave-2d}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{examples/wave:module-examples.wave}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Conservative 2D anisotropic membrane with mixed boundary ports.

\sphinxAtStartPar
2D mixed\sphinxhyphen{}boundary anisotropic membrane, energy variables q=grad w,
p=rho*w\_t, coenergy e\_q=T q and e\_p=p/rho. This preserves the
original model’s four boundary ports and its actual GetFEM GWFL
Hamiltonian 0.5*q.T.q, where T is the full tensor parameter.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Physical outward\sphinxhyphen{}normal traction: u\_N=n.e\_q at bottom/right/top;
observation y\_N=e\_p. Left side prescribes u\_D=e\_p (velocity) and
observes y\_D=n.e\_q (traction). The pH energy balance is
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
H(t)\sphinxhyphen{}H(0) = integral (u\_N*y\_N + u\_D*y\_D) dt.
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The negative flow\sphinxhyphen{}side algebraic rows impose Y\_N=e\_p and U\_D=e\_p:
this is the same physical sign convention as qualified wave\_1d.py.
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{physical} sign of the measured work is audited independently
against the original GetFEM Hamiltonian; no success is inferred
solely from these formulae.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This tutorial starts from EXACTLY zero, compatible with zero
initial Dirichlet velocity and initial normal stress, and uses
a left\sphinxhyphen{}boundary velocity that is zero at t=0 but nontrivial soon
after. The original model, before promotion, passed real MUMPS MPI1/2
10\sphinxhyphen{}step TSCN physical and shared\sphinxhyphen{}ParaView tests at cf42089d;
other LU backends require independent native acceptance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Scientific context: Haine, Matignon, Serhani (2023), anisotropic
heterogeneous wave PFEM, DOI 10.4208/ijnam2023\sphinxhyphen{}1005; and
Brugnoli, Haine, Matignon (2022) on mixed boundary control.

\subsubsection{Why this example?}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave:why-this-example}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{started::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{first tutorial}}}} showed a \sphinxstylestrong{one\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional}
string and its two boundary ports. Our next model is genuinely
\sphinxstylestrong{two\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional}, heterogeneous and anisotropic, with \sphinxstylestrong{mixed
boundary control}: three boundary segments prescribe an outward
normal traction, while the fourth prescribes a \sphinxstyleemphasis{velocity}. We will
keep exactly the same materials, mesh and boundary convention when
we add an internal dissipative port in example \sphinxstylestrong{2B}. We will
then study the complementary co\sphinxhyphen{}energy formulation in example
\sphinxstylestrong{2C} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{examples/wave_coenergy::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{The wave equation — 2C: co\sphinxhyphen{}energy and localized damping}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This page describes the actual code in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/wave.py}}.
Its snippets are included \sphinxstylestrong{directly from that file}, avoiding
manual discrepancies between the tutorial and the program.
The validated source is the same for all PETSc solver backends.


\subsubsection{The physical model}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave:the-physical-model}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Let \(\Omega=(0,2)\times(0,1)\) and let \(w(t,x,y)\)
denote the transverse displacement of a membrane. We consider
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\rho(x)\,\partial_{tt} w
- \operatorname{div}(T(x,y)\nabla w)=0,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where the in\sphinxhyphen{}plane tension tensor and areal mass density are
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}T(x,y)=\begin{bmatrix}5+x&xy\\xy&2+y\end{bmatrix},
\qquad \rho(x)=3-x.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Here \(T\) is \sphinxstylestrong{not} a scalar Young modulus. It is a
symmetric, positive\sphinxhyphen{}definite anisotropic tensor; both \(T\)
and \(\rho\) vary spatially. The lower, right and upper
boundaries are \(\Gamma_N\) (GetFEM regions 10, 11 and 12).
The left boundary is \(\Gamma_D\) (region 13). Writing
\(n\) for the \sphinxstylestrong{outward} unit normal, the controls are
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}n\cdot(T\nabla w)=u_N \quad\hbox{on }\Gamma_N,
\qquad \partial_t w=u_D \quad\hbox{on }\Gamma_D.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The second condition prescribes \sphinxstyleemphasis{velocity}, \sphinxstylestrong{not} displacement.
This is sometimes called a velocity\sphinxhyphen{}Dirichlet port in the
port\sphinxhyphen{}Hamiltonian literature.


\subsubsection{Energy variables, co\sphinxhyphen{}energy variables and power}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave:energy-variables-co-energy-variables-and-power}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
We choose the energy states
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}q=\nabla w,\qquad p=\rho\,\partial_t w,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and their conjugate co\sphinxhyphen{}energies
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}e_q=Tq,\qquad e_p=p/\rho.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Thus \(q\) and \(e_q\) are \sphinxstylestrong{vectors},
whereas \(p\) and \(e_p\) are \sphinxstylestrong{scalars}. The
first\sphinxhyphen{}order port\sphinxhyphen{}Hamiltonian dynamics are
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\partial_t q=\nabla e_p,\qquad
\partial_t p=\operatorname{div}e_q.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The physical Hamiltonian is
\begin{equation}\label{equation:examples/wave:wave_2d_conservative_energy}
\begin{split}\mathcal H(q,p)=\tfrac12\int_{\Omega}
\left(q\cdot Tq+\frac{p^2}{\rho}\right)\,\mathrm dx.\end{split}
\end{equation}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In the \sphinxstylestrong{GetFEM Generic Weak Form Language} (GWFL),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{q.T.q}} denotes \(q\cdot Tq\): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{T}} is the
\sphinxstylestrong{tensor parameter’s identifier}, not the transpose
operator from Python/NumPy. The actual code therefore
correctly uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"0.5*q.T.q"}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
With our boundary orientation, the collocated outputs are
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}y_N=e_p \quad\hbox{on }\Gamma_N,\qquad
y_D=n\cdot e_q \quad\hbox{on }\Gamma_D.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The energy exchanged with the environment is
\begin{equation}\label{equation:examples/wave:wave_2d_conservative_power}
\begin{split}\frac{\mathrm d\mathcal H}{\mathrm dt}
=\int_{\Gamma_N}u_N y_N\,\mathrm ds
 +\int_{\Gamma_D}u_D y_D\,\mathrm ds.\end{split}
\end{equation}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Our short demonstration uses \sphinxstylestrong{zero} Neumann tractions,
with a nontrivial prescribed left velocity. Thus the
left\sphinxhyphen{}hand boundary supplies the entire mechanical work;
the right, top and bottom boundary powers are zero.


\subsubsection{From the strong equation to PFEM}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave:from-the-strong-equation-to-pfem}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Integrating \(\partial_t p=\operatorname{div}e_q\)
against a test function \(\varphi_p\) gives
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\int_\Omega\partial_t p\,\varphi_p
=-\int_\Omega e_q\cdot\nabla\varphi_p
 +\int_{\Gamma_N}u_N\varphi_p
 +\int_{\Gamma_D}y_D\varphi_p.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The first equation is tested without integration by parts:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\int_\Omega\partial_t q\cdot\varphi_q
=\int_\Omega\nabla e_p\cdot\varphi_q.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These two choices yield the partitioned finite\sphinxhyphen{}element
discretization (PFEM): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DG1}} for vector strain
\(q\), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CG2}} for scalar momentum \(p\),
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DG1}} boundary traces. The exact finite\sphinxhyphen{}element
spaces and material definitions are shown below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In SCRIMP’s assembly convention, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{flow\sphinxhyphen{}side}
algebraic variables for the Neumann velocity observations
are \sphinxstylestrong{\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}\sphinxhyphen{}Y\_B\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}, \textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}\sphinxhyphen{}Y\_R\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}, \textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}\sphinxhyphen{}Y\_T\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}}, and the
velocity input on the left appears as \sphinxstylestrong{\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}\sphinxhyphen{}U\_L\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}}.
The corresponding effort\sphinxhyphen{}side test terms are negative
velocity traces. The signs make the measured
powers consistent with \eqref{equation:examples/wave:wave_2d_conservative_power}.
They have been checked by native GetFEM/PETSc simulations,
not merely assumed from the matrix layout.

\sphinxstylestrong{5. Prescribe compatible initial data and controls.}
We set \(q_0=p_0=0\), so \(e_q=e_p=0\)
at the initial instant, and apply
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}u_D(t,y)=0.2\sin(4\pi t)\sin(\pi y).\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This input also vanishes at \(t=0\) and at the
corners of the left boundary. It is already nonzero
during the ten\sphinxhyphen{}step installation smoke.

    \PYG{n}{ts\PYGZus{}exact\PYGZus{}final\PYGZus{}time}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{matchstep}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{ksp\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{gmres}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{pc\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{lu}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{t\PYGZus{}0}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{t\PYGZus{}f}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{final\PYGZus{}time}\PYG{p}{,}

    \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{system}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{solve}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Installation and genuine scientific checks}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave:installation-and-genuine-scientific-checks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The result must be a real \sphinxstylestrong{GetFEM/PETSc} solve, not an LU
factorization smoke. The common \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{measure\_wave\_2d()}}
function checks convergence, the strict initial DAE
projection, nonzero left power and the mechanical
energy/work equality \sphinxstylestrong{at every accepted CN step}:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathcal H(t_k)-\mathcal H(t_{k-1})
-\Delta t_k\left(P_{B,k}+P_{R,k}+P_{T,k}+P_{L,k}\right)
\simeq 0.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The port powers \(P_{\ast,k}\) are the genuine
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cn\_step}} GetFEM integrals sampled on the \sphinxstylestrong{mean FE
state} of the accepted step, not instantaneous endpoint
powers. Never trapezoid\sphinxhyphen{}integrate the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P{[}0{]}}} sample.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstylestrong{initial MUMPS native pilot} passed in MPI 1
and MPI 2, with 2,230 DOFs, ten accepted steps and
numerical energy/power defects below
\(3\times10^{-18}\). Both ranks had identical
full trajectories; the MPI 1/MPI 2 state difference
was below \(4.2\times10^{-14}\). All four
fields (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{q}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\_q}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\_p}})
were exported as valid, root\sphinxhyphen{}only shared VTU/PVD,
with \sphinxstylestrong{11 time frames per field}. This is a
qualified \sphinxstylestrong{MUMPS MPI1/2} result only, not yet
a five\sphinxhyphen{}backend installation acceptance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The complete installation acceptance requires:
MUMPS (MPI 1/2), sequential SuperLU (MPI 1),
and SuperLU\_DIST (MPI 1/2). The three backends
must reproduce the same state, Hamiltonian,
physical powers, and ParaView outputs.
SuperLU standard is \sphinxstylestrong{serial\sphinxhyphen{}only}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To save the four original GetFEM variable series,
open \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{outputs/my\_wave\_2d/pv/q/q.pvd}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pv/p/p.pvd}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pv/e\_q/e\_q.pvd}} or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pv/e\_p/e\_p.pvd}} in ParaView and play the
11 frames. The vector fields \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{q}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\_q}} may be displayed with arrows; the
velocity is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\_p}} (not momentum \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p}}).


\paragraph{Longer native showcase: 100\sphinxhyphen{}step energy and wave propagation}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave:longer-native-showcase-100-step-energy-and-wave-propagation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{PASS, 25 November 2026}, on the complete original
GetFEM/PETSc MUMPS MPI1 archive
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{v130\sphinxhyphen{}wave2d\sphinxhyphen{}2a\sphinxhyphen{}showcase\sphinxhyphen{}bd6f5468\sphinxhyphen{}teEK1Ejz.zip}}
(source \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bd6f5468e3a167f2b2a3b9e1b72bcc54e1948d45}},
native Docker image \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scrimp\sphinxhyphen{}mpi:v1.3.0\sphinxhyphen{}rc3}}).
This longer visual run used \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{h=0.1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dt=0.01}}
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tf=1}}, with \sphinxstylestrong{8,138 DOFs}, \sphinxstylestrong{100/100
accepted fixed Crank\textendash{}Nicolson steps}, zero
rejections, exact DAE initialization, and
\sphinxstylestrong{7/7 original physical acceptance gates passed}.
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathcal H(0)=0,\qquad
\mathcal H(1)=0.03707053141235693,\qquad
W_{\partial}(1)=0.03707053141235698.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstylestrong{open conservative} boundary\sphinxhyphen{}work balance
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{H(t)\sphinxhyphen{}H(0)=W\_boundary(t)}} holds at each
accepted CN step (maximum absolute defect
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2.07e\sphinxhyphen{}16}}) and cumulatively (maximum
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.25e\sphinxhyphen{}16}}). The \sphinxstyleemphasis{left imposed\sphinxhyphen{}velocity
port} supplies the energy; all three other
Neumann boundaries carry exactly zero power.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The original \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rank0.npz}} is accompanied by
\sphinxstylestrong{four PVD series and 404 authentic GetFEM VTU
files}, for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{q}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\_q}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\_p}},
each at \sphinxstylestrong{101 times} from 0 to 1.
The renderer generated from the actual FE data:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{visuals/field\_snapshots.\{png,svg\}}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{visuals/energy\_balance.\{png,svg\}}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{visuals/p\_evolution.gif}} (101 frames),
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{visuals/energy\_and\_ports.csv}}, plus a
machine\sphinxhyphen{}readable provenance JSON. The animation
shows a boundary\sphinxhyphen{}generated disturbance
propagating through the anisotropic rectangle.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interpretation of fields matters:}
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{q=Grad(w)}} is the \sphinxstyleemphasis{displacement gradient}
(not stress), while \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p=rho*dt(w)}} is \sphinxstyleemphasis{momentum}
(not velocity). The velocity is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\_p=p/rho}},
and the stress\sphinxhyphen{}like energy co\sphinxhyphen{}variable is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\_q=T*q}}. The generic maps and GIF currently
display \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{p}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|q|}}; they must not be
labeled velocity or stress. The original
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\_p}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\_q}} VTK series permit these
physical quantities to be visualized separately.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To reproduce the independently qualified
long MUMPS MPI1 visual run:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZti{}/Simulations/scrimp
git\PYG{+w}{ }pull\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}ff\PYGZhy{}only
conda\PYG{+w}{ }activate\PYG{+w}{ }scrimp
\PYG{n+nv}{SCRIMP\PYGZus{}DOCKER\PYGZus{}NO\PYGZus{}SUDO}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{n+nv}{SCRIMP\PYGZus{}V130\PYGZus{}DAE\PYGZus{}IMAGE}\PYG{o}{=}scrimp\PYGZhy{}mpi:v1.3.0\PYGZhy{}rc3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
bash\PYG{+w}{ }scripts/run\PYGZhy{}v130\PYGZhy{}wave2d\PYGZhy{}showcase.sh\PYG{+w}{ }2a
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This long\sphinxhyphen{}run result is \sphinxstylestrong{not an MPI1/MPI2 parity
test or a mesh/time convergence study}. The short
MUMPS MPI1/2 and other solver installation
acceptance remains a separate experiment.
The displacement \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{w}} is not an independent
state of this energy\sphinxhyphen{}based DAE; any animation
of it must identify its reconstruction
method and gauge.


\subsubsection{Scientific references}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave:scientific-references}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This introductory 2D example illustrates the
PFEM framework analyzed by \sphinxstylestrong{Haine, Matignon and
Serhani (2023)}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Numerical Analysis of a
Structure\sphinxhyphen{}Preserving Space\sphinxhyphen{}Discretization for an
Anisotropic and Heterogeneous Boundary Controlled
N\sphinxhyphen{}Dimensional Wave Equation As a Port\sphinxhyphen{}Hamiltonian
System}, DOI \sphinxtitleref{10.4208/ijnam2023\sphinxhyphen{}1005}, and
the mixed\sphinxhyphen{}boundary\sphinxhyphen{}control work of \sphinxstylestrong{Brugnoli,
Haine and Matignon (2022)}. The tutorial is
\sphinxstylestrong{not} a numerical reproduction of either paper.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The next section introduces a physically distinct
\sphinxstylestrong{resistive port} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/wave\_dissipative.py}}
while keeping the same material, domain and
conventions. The later {\hyperref[\detokenize{examples/wave_coenergy::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{The wave equation — 2C: co\sphinxhyphen{}energy and localized damping}}}}
chapter changes the state variables and adds
spatially localized damping.


\subsubsection{2B — Adding a resistive port: heterogeneous damping}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave:module-examples.wave_dissipative}}\label{\detokenize{examples/wave:b-adding-a-resistive-port-heterogeneous-damping}}\index{module@\spxentry{module}!examples.wave\_dissipative@\spxentry{examples.wave\_dissipative}}\index{examples.wave\_dissipative@\spxentry{examples.wave\_dissipative}!module@\spxentry{module}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dissipative 2D anisotropic membrane with mixed boundary ports.

\sphinxAtStartPar
2D mixed\sphinxhyphen{}boundary anisotropic membrane, energy variables q=grad w,
p=rho*w\_t, coenergy e\_q=T q and e\_p=p/rho. This preserves the
original model’s four boundary ports and its actual GetFEM GWFL
Hamiltonian 0.5*q.T.q, where T is the full tensor parameter.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Physical outward\sphinxhyphen{}normal traction: u\_N=n.e\_q at bottom/right/top;
observation y\_N=e\_p. Left side prescribes u\_D=e\_p (velocity) and
observes y\_D=n.e\_q (traction). The physical pH energy balance is
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
H(t)\sphinxhyphen{}H(0) = W\_boundary(t) \sphinxhyphen{} integral\_0\textasciicircum{}t D(s) ds.
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The signed algebraic boundary rows impose Y\_N=e\_p and U\_D=e\_p.
The additional port obeys f\_r=\sphinxhyphen{}e\_p, e\_r=nu*f\_r with nu\textgreater{}=0.
Thus its positive dissipated power is e\_r*f\_r=nu*f\_r*f\_r and
dH/dt = signed\_boundary\_work\_rate \sphinxhyphen{} integral\_Omega(nu*f\_r*f\_r).
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{physical} sign of the measured work is audited independently
against the original GetFEM Hamiltonian; no success is inferred
solely from these formulae.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As in qualified 2A, the initial strain and momentum are exactly zero,
the left velocity input starts at zero, and the tensor, density,
boundary mesh and 10\sphinxhyphen{}step CN discretization are unchanged.
The only new physics is nu(x)=damping\_strength*0.5*(2\sphinxhyphen{}x)\textgreater{}=0.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Scientific context: Haine, Matignon, Serhani (2023), anisotropic
heterogeneous wave PFEM, DOI 10.4208/ijnam2023\sphinxhyphen{}1005; and
Brugnoli, Haine, Matignon (2022) on mixed boundary control.

\paragraph{What changes relative to 2A?}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave:what-changes-relative-to-2a}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This second example introduces \sphinxstylestrong{one new physical feature}:
distributed viscous damping of the 2D anisotropic membrane.
The independent, executable source is
\sphinxtitleref{examples/wave\_dissipative.py}. Its rectangle,
material tensor, density, normal directions, four boundary
control ports, finite\sphinxhyphen{}element spaces for \sphinxtitleref{q} and \sphinxtitleref{p},
initial conditions and fixed Crank\textendash{}Nicolson scheme
are \sphinxstyleemphasis{identical} to those of {\hyperref[\detokenize{examples/wave::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{The wave equation — 2A: conservative anisotropic membrane}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
On \(\Omega=(0,2)\times(0,1)\), the equation now reads
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\rho(x)\,\partial_{tt}w
-\operatorname{div}(T(x,y)\nabla w)
+\nu(x)\,\partial_t w=0,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with the same symmetric positive\sphinxhyphen{}definite tension and mass as
example 2A and the additional nonnegative, spatially varying
damping coefficient
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\nu(x)=\tfrac12(2-x)\geq0.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The damping is nonzero throughout the interior except on the
right boundary. We may choose a nonnegative strength multiplier
in the executable; the default is \sphinxtitleref{damping\_strength=1.0}.
\sphinxstylestrong{Damping does not change the Hamiltonian:}
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathcal H(q,p)=\tfrac12\int_\Omega
\left(q\cdot Tq+\frac{p^2}{\rho}\right)\,\mathrm dx.\end{split}
\end{equation*}

\paragraph{Why add a separate resistive port?}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave:why-add-a-separate-resistive-port}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
We retain the \sphinxstyleemphasis{skew\sphinxhyphen{}adjoint} interconnection of 2A and
expose the dissipation as a new scalar algebraic port
\sphinxtitleref{(f\_r,e\_r)}. The state and co\sphinxhyphen{}energy variables are still
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}q=\nabla w,\quad p=\rho\,\partial_t w,\qquad
e_q=Tq,\quad e_p=p/\rho.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The additional constitutive and coupling equations are
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}f_r=-e_p,\qquad e_r=\nu f_r,\end{split}
\end{equation*}\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{pmatrix}\partial_t q\\ \partial_t p\\ f_r\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
0&\nabla&0\\
\operatorname{div}&0&I\\
0&-I&0
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}e_q\\e_p\\e_r\end{pmatrix}.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Indeed, \sphinxtitleref{e\_r=\sphinxhyphen{}nu e\_p} and
\sphinxtitleref{partial\_t p=operatorname\{div\}e\_q\sphinxhyphen{}nu e\_p}.
The discrete resistive port introduces \sphinxstylestrong{two algebraic
fields} \sphinxtitleref{f\_r} and \sphinxtitleref{e\_r} (both CG2), while
preserving the mechanical variables and boundary ports
from example 2A.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The dissipation power is \sphinxstyleemphasis{positive}:
\begin{equation}\label{equation:examples/wave:wave2b_dissipated_power}
\begin{split}D(t)=\int_\Omega f_r\,e_r\,\mathrm dx
    =\int_\Omega \nu\,f_r^2\,\mathrm dx\geq0.\end{split}
\end{equation}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consequently, for the same boundary work
\(W_\partial(t)\) as 2A,
\begin{equation}\label{equation:examples/wave:wave2b_energy_dissipation}
\begin{split}\mathcal H(t)-\mathcal H(0)
= W_\partial(t)-\int_0^t D(s)\,\mathrm ds.\end{split}
\end{equation}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A dissipative system can \sphinxstylestrong{still gain mechanical energy}
if its boundary ports inject more power than it dissipates.
The correct identity is therefore
\(\Delta H=W_\partial-L_\nu\), \sphinxstyleemphasis{not}
the unconditional monotonicity of \(H\).


\paragraph{Build the actual GetFEM/PETSc model}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave:build-the-actual-getfem-petsc-model}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following code fragments are \sphinxstylestrong{read directly from}
\sphinxtitleref{examples/wave\_dissipative.py}; they are not second,
manually maintained versions of the solver.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{1. Construct the same 2D physical and co\sphinxhyphen{}energy states:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{system} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{S}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{DPHS}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{real}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\eqref{equation:examples/wave:wave2b_dissipated_power}.

\paragraph{Physical qualification: original boundary work minus dissipation}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave:physical-qualification-original-boundary-work-minus-dissipation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For each \sphinxstyleemphasis{accepted} CN step, the program measures the original
GetFEM Hamiltonian and all four port powers on the \sphinxstylestrong{mean
finite\sphinxhyphen{}element state}. The resistive power is computed by
SCRIMP’s native \sphinxtitleref{Port.compute()}, and checked independently
by a second GetFEM volume quadrature of \sphinxtitleref{nu*f\_r*f\_r}.
The intended stepwise residual is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathcal R_k
=\mathcal H_k-\mathcal H_{k-1}
-\Delta t_k\sum_{\Gamma}P_{\Gamma,k}
+\Delta t_k D_k \simeq0.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The script also verifies the cumulative
\eqref{equation:examples/wave:wave2b_energy_dissipation}, the nonnegativity
of the actual dissipated power, the resistive
flow equation, and the consistency of the
11\sphinxhyphen{}snapshot accepted FE history. Because
\sphinxtitleref{nu f\_r} has higher polynomial degree than
the CG2 space of \sphinxtitleref{e\_r}, the constitutive
relationship is \sphinxstylestrong{discrete weak projection};
a pointwise zero \sphinxtitleref{L\textasciicircum{}2} error is \sphinxstylestrong{not}
an appropriate acceptance criterion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Run a short, \sphinxstyleemphasis{real} GetFEM/PETSc check (not a
standalone LU smoke):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\sphinxstylestrong{2B has 13.528\% less mechanical energy}
than 2A at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{t=1}}. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{applied control is
identical}, but the \sphinxstyleemphasis{work delivered} need not
be: it depends on the dynamical response.
Consequently the difference in stored energy
is not exactly the dissipated energy.
The exact comparison identity is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathcal H_{2A}-\mathcal H_{2B}
= L_{2B} - (W_{2B}-W_{2A}),\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
which matches the real GetFEM values to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2.08e\sphinxhyphen{}17}}. This distinction matters when
illustrating dissipation in an \sphinxstylestrong{open}
port\sphinxhyphen{}Hamiltonian system.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Audit actual CN midpoint FE work, damping and boundary feedback.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here the signed algebraic boundary power U*Y is a LOSS: because
the coenergy Grad\sphinxhyphen{}Grad coupling imposes Y=\sphinxhyphen{}p (weakly), the original
FE balance is dH/dt=\sphinxhyphen{}integral(U*Y)\sphinxhyphen{}D\_r. The passive law is U=+kY.
This is not the mixed\sphinxhyphen{}boundary 2A/2B sign convention.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The substituted resistive port has \sphinxstyleemphasis{no} independent flow unknown and
Port.get\_power() correctly cannot report its dissipative power.
We assemble its true mixed FE dissipation in two mathematically
equivalent ways: D\_r=integral e\_r**2/nu = \sphinxhyphen{}integral p*e\_r.
The pointwise nu*p**2 is ONLY a diagnostic because e\_r is DG1 and
nu*p is not generally in the same FE space.

\subsubsection{Why this third tutorial?}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave_coenergy:why-this-third-tutorial}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tutorial {\hyperref[\detokenize{examples/wave::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{The wave equation — 2A: conservative anisotropic membrane}}}} introduces the \sphinxstylestrong{anisotropic 2D membrane and
mixed boundary ports} (2A), then a \sphinxstylestrong{separate resistive flow/effort
pair} (2B). This tutorial introduces a genuinely different
construction: the \sphinxstylestrong{co\sphinxhyphen{}energy states} themselves, a \sphinxstylestrong{concentric
two\sphinxhyphen{}region domain}, inner damping and an outer boundary feedback.
It does not replace 2A or 2B or imply identical meshes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The actual, executable code is
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/wave\_coenergy.py}}. Fragments below are included from
that file, rather than copied into the documentation. The short
default example (\sphinxtitleref{h=0.2, dt=0.008, tf=0.08}) is a \sphinxstylestrong{qualified native
MUMPS MPI1/2 acceptance pilot}, not a resolved wave\sphinxhyphen{}propagation
demonstration or a convergence study.


\subsubsection{The true material inverse}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave_coenergy:the-true-material-inverse}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The physical tension and density retain the definitions of 2A/2B:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}T(x,y)=\begin{bmatrix}5+x&xy\\xy&2+y\end{bmatrix},
\qquad \rho(x)=3-x.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
However, the co\sphinxhyphen{}energy formulation needs the actual compliance,
\sphinxstylestrong{not} the same numeric tensor renamed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Tinv}}:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}T^{-1}(x,y)=\frac{1}{(5+x)(2+y)-(xy)^2}
\begin{bmatrix}2+y&-xy\\-xy&5+x\end{bmatrix}.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
On the unit disk the determinant is strictly positive. The
GetFEM GWFL parameter \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Tinv}} below encodes this inverse;
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{q.Tinv.q}} is a tensor contraction, not a Python transpose.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The co\sphinxhyphen{}energy unknowns are now \sphinxstylestrong{stress} \sphinxtitleref{q=T grad(w)}
and \sphinxstylestrong{velocity} \sphinxtitleref{p=dw/dt}. The conjugate co\sphinxhyphen{}states have
been substituted, so they do not introduce extra FE unknowns.
The mechanical energy is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathcal H(q,p)=\frac12\int_\Omega
\left(q\cdot T^{-1}q+\rho p^2\right)\,\mathrm dx.\end{split}
\end{equation*}

\subsubsection{Two regions and substituted ports}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave_coenergy:two-regions-and-substituted-ports}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The geometry is a unit disk split into the inner disk
\sphinxtitleref{Omega\_1} (radius 0.6, region 1) and an annulus
\sphinxtitleref{Omega\_2} (region 2). Region 10 is their interface;
region 20 is the external boundary. The damping port
is present \sphinxstylestrong{only} on region 1 and the boundary port
\sphinxstylestrong{only} on region 20.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set the domain (using the built\PYGZhy{}in geometry `Concentric`)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Labels: Disk = 1, Annulus = 2, Interface = 10, Boundary = 20}
    \PYG{n}{omega} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{S}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Domain}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Concentric}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{R}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{r}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.6}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{h}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{mesh\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{mesh\PYGZus{}output\PYGZus{}dir}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{wave}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}output\PYGZus{}path}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{mesh}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{n}{create}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxtitleref{nu\textasciicircum{}\{\sphinxhyphen{}1\} e\_r = \sphinxhyphen{}p} in its finite\sphinxhyphen{}element weak form.
Unlike a non\sphinxhyphen{}substituted port, it has no independent
GetFEM flow variable. Consequently its power \sphinxstylestrong{cannot}
be obtained through \sphinxtitleref{Port.get\_power()}. The native audit
instead evaluates the original FE functions by independent
GetFEM quadrature.

The legacy coefficient \sphinxtitleref{nu=10(0.36\sphinxhyphen{}r\textasciicircum{}2)} vanished at
the interface even though a brick integrates \sphinxtitleref{1/nu}.
Here we deliberately use
\sphinxtitleref{nu=0.2+10(0.36\sphinxhyphen{}r\textasciicircum{}2)} \sphinxstylestrong{on region 1 only}.
This is a strictly positive, bounded invertible
coefficient on the disk and still has exactly zero
damping on the outer annulus by region restriction.
It is a documented change to the legacy scenario,
not a numerical regularization hidden in SCRIMP.

\subsubsection{The co\sphinxhyphen{}energy balance and feedback sign}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave_coenergy:the-co-energy-balance-and-feedback-sign}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The semidiscrete system is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}T^{-1}\dot q=\nabla p,\qquad
\rho\dot p=\operatorname{div}q+e_r
\quad (e_r\text{ acts only on }\Omega_1),\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with the \sphinxstylestrong{signed Grad\textendash{}Grad boundary observation}
\sphinxtitleref{Y=\sphinxhyphen{}p} (in the boundary FE weak sense). The trace is
not the \sphinxtitleref{Y=p} used in an alternative boundary\sphinxhyphen{}port
orientation. The algebraic signed port power reported
by SCRIMP is \sphinxtitleref{P\_b=integral UY}, and the original
co\sphinxhyphen{}energy Dirac bricks give
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\frac{\mathrm d\mathcal H}{\mathrm dt}
=-\int_{\partial\Omega} UY\,\mathrm ds
 -\int_{\Omega_1}\frac{e_r^2}{\nu}\,\mathrm dx.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Consequently the passive control is \textasciigrave{}U=+0.5Y\textasciigrave{}}:
\sphinxtitleref{P\_b=+0.5*integral Y\textasciicircum{}2 \textgreater{}= 0}, and this port power
is \sphinxstylestrong{subtracted} from the Hamiltonian. A previous
trial mistakenly used \sphinxtitleref{U=\sphinxhyphen{}0.5Y}: the unqualified
real MUMPS MPI1/2 archive
\sphinxtitleref{v130\sphinxhyphen{}wave2d\sphinxhyphen{}coenergy\sphinxhyphen{}e1c5bc50\sphinxhyphen{}bRo68Qaf.zip}
proved that law injected energy. Its measured identity
was \sphinxtitleref{H\sphinxhyphen{}H0+Li\sphinxhyphen{}Lb=0} to 1e\sphinxhyphen{}15, with the entire rejected
energy defect equal to twice the signed boundary work.
This is a physical sign correction, \sphinxstylestrong{not} an adjustment
to energy tolerances or an arbitrary renaming of power.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For the two dissipative mechanisms, define
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}D_i=\int_{\Omega_1}\frac{e_r^2}{\nu}\,\mathrm dx
   =-\int_{\Omega_1}p e_r\,\mathrm dx\ge0,
\qquad
D_b=\int_{\partial\Omega} UY\,\mathrm ds
   =0.5\int_{\partial\Omega}Y^2\,\mathrm ds\ge0.\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The equality for \sphinxtitleref{D\_i} holds \sphinxstylestrong{in the FE weak
projection}. The pointwise integral \sphinxtitleref{integral nu*p\textasciicircum{}2}
need not agree exactly, because \sphinxtitleref{e\_r} is DG1, and
\sphinxtitleref{nu*p} generally is not. We record it as a diagnostic,
not a false exactness gate.

\sphinxAtStartPar
There is no independent boundary drive in this scenario;
therefore the physical balance to validate is
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\boxed{\mathcal H(t)-\mathcal H(0)+
\int_0^t (D_i(s)+D_b(s))\,\mathrm ds=0.}\end{split}
\end{equation*}

\subsubsection{A physically visible initial pulse}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave_coenergy:a-physically-visible-initial-pulse}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Two smooth initial velocity bumps excite the inner
damping and outer feedback. The initial stress is zero.
The time integrator is \sphinxstylestrong{fixed Crank\textendash{}Nicolson}, ten
accepted steps, with algebraic DAE initialization
and default MUMPS LU. The short time interval proves
the simulation and output pipeline works, but does
not by itself establish long\sphinxhyphen{}time spatial quality.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}\PYGZsh{} Initialize the problem}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} The controls expression}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} The Grad\PYGZhy{}Grad boundary output has Y=\PYGZhy{}p (weak trace):}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} its signed port power is U*Y and dH/dt=\PYGZhy{}U*Y\PYGZhy{}D\PYGZus{}internal.}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Thus U=+kY is passive: U*Y=+k*Y**2 and dH/dt\PYGZlt{}=0.}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} The previous U=\PYGZhy{}kY *injected* energy, as proved by native CN}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} H+L\PYGZus{}internal\PYGZhy{}L\PYGZus{}boundary=0 (e1c5bc50, MPI1/MPI2).}
    \PYG{n}{expressions} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{FEEDBACK\PYGZus{}GAIN}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{*Y}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
    
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add each expression to its control\PYGZus{}port}
    \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{control\PYGZus{}port}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{expression} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{zip}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{control\PYGZus{}ports}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{expressions}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set the control functions (automatic construction of bricks such that \PYGZhy{}M\PYGZus{}u u + f(t) = 0)}
        \PYG{n}{wave}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}control}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{control\PYGZus{}port}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{expression}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set the initial data}
    \PYG{n}{wave}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}initial\PYGZus{}value}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{q}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{[0., 0.]}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Smooth two\PYGZhy{}part velocity pulse excites both internal damping and the}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} exterior feedback already at t=0, without prescribing a boundary trace.}
    \PYG{n}{wave}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}initial\PYGZus{}value}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{p}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{exp(\PYGZhy{}10*(x*x+y*y))+0.4*exp(\PYGZhy{}15*((x\PYGZhy{}0.8)*(x\PYGZhy{}0.8)+y*y))}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{)}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}\PYGZsh{} Solve in time}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Define the time scheme (\PYGZdq{}cn\PYGZdq{} is Crank\PYGZhy{}Nicolson)}
    \PYG{n}{options} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{factor\PYGZus{}solver} \PYG{o+ow}{is} \PYG{o+ow}{not} \PYG{k+kc}{None}\PYG{p}{:}

        \PYG{n}{ts\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{cn}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ts\PYGZus{}adapt\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{none}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{ts\PYGZus{}exact\PYGZus{}final\PYGZus{}time}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{matchstep}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}

        \PYG{n}{t\PYGZus{}0}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{t\PYGZus{}f}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{final\PYGZus{}time}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{dt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{time\PYGZus{}step}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{dt\PYGZus{}save}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{time\PYGZus{}step}\PYG{p}{,}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subsubsection{Native outputs and visualizations}
\label{\detokenize{examples/wave_coenergy:native-outputs-and-visualizations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The pilot below records the original \sphinxstylestrong{full FE state
history} in NPZ, true GetFEM Hamiltonian and power
histories, detailed JSON physical gates, two independent
quadratures of inner resistance, and GetFEM/ParaView
time series \sphinxtitleref{q}, \sphinxtitleref{p}, \sphinxtitleref{e\_r} (one PVD and eleven VTU
per field and MPI case). It checks strict DAE, CN
work/loss balance at every step, nontrivial passive
feedback and damping, MPI replica/parity, and genuine
nonempty VTK fields.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Once a native case passes, the same script renders
\sphinxstylestrong{from the original FE NPZ/VTK}, not an invented
analytic image:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{visuals/energy\_balance.png}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.svg}}:
mechanical energy vs work/losses, powers, balance defect;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{visuals/field\_snapshots.png}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.svg}}:
spatial snapshots of \sphinxtitleref{p}, \sphinxtitleref{|q|}, \sphinxtitleref{e\_r};

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{visuals/p\_evolution.gif}}: animated accepted \sphinxtitleref{p}
snapshots (pilot: 11 frames);

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{visuals/energy\_and\_ports.csv}}: actual energetic
histories with explicit columns;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{visuals/provenance.json}}: commit, image revision,
number of frames and Float32 VTK warning.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Open \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mumps\_mpi1/pv/p/p.pvd}} (or q/e\_r) in
ParaView to examine the whole native sequence. VTK
Float32 is for visualisation; the acceptance audit
uses full\sphinxhyphen{}precision original GetFEM FE values.

conda\PYG{+w}{ }activate\PYG{+w}{ }scrimp

\PYG{n+nv}{SCRIMP\PYGZus{}DOCKER\PYGZus{}NO\PYGZus{}SUDO}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{n+nv}{SCRIMP\PYGZus{}V130\PYGZus{}DAE\PYGZus{}IMAGE}\PYG{o}{=}scrimp\PYGZhy{}mpi:v1.3.0\PYGZhy{}rc3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
